title: Signature Improvement Candidate Record
body:
Overview

This record belongs to the Safe Self-Improvement and Rollback Signature Database (Signature edition), Manon's original counterpart to the public database of the same name. The Signature edition does not copy any public product: it restates the subject in Manon's own Signature framing, as a design that lives inside the Signature ecosystem. Improvement Candidate Record covers the following in Signature terms: describes a proposed improvement, its source experiment, and the gates it must pass. The record is written as a complete, usable file, with a demo program genuinely executed at build time and its output stored beside the code. Benchmark honesty: this database defines part of the fixed test suite for the R32 capability collection. Its target is 99% measured reliability on defined tasks (TARGET, not measured result). The comparative measurement run comes after building and is not claimed anywhere in this round.

How the Signature design works

The Signature design works like this: a candidate improvement is tested in stages against the fixed suite and the regression suite, and it is promoted only when it passes every gate; if a promoted change later fails its triggers, the recorded rollback procedure restores the last known-good version. Applied to this record, the design means the following in practice: describes a proposed improvement, its source experiment, and the gates it must pass. The record sits at ladder rank simple in the teaching ladder, which runs simple, then compounded, then most complex, so a Signature reader can start from the simpler records and work toward this one.

Worked example

The demo compares a candidate gate score with the known-good gate score and prints the promotion decision. The demo program prints:

Candidate gate score: 78 points
Known-good gate score: 80 points
Decision: HOLD (rollback target stays pinned)

Use and limits

Staged testing reduces risk but never removes it. A candidate can pass every gate on the fixed tasks and still fail on unseen tasks, which is why rollback triggers stay armed after promotion. In Signature practice, a reader can use this record to run the same check inside the Signature ecosystem: follow the design, compare the result with the worked example, and record any difference with its evidence. The record is one of sixteen in this Signature database, and it cross-links to related databases so the reader can continue from here.
